subject: Handshake window for engineering workshop (NA / EMEA / APAC)
messages:
From: Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@acme-oss.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Sørensen <anika.sorensen@acme-oss.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:12:00 +0100
Subject: Engineering workshop — aligning windows across NA/EMEA/APAC

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. The engineering leads at Acme want a focused 90–120 minute technical workshop (solutions + our platform architects) to walk through integration patterns, expected throughput, and the KV cache behavior under our workload. We need SE presence (one of your engineers) plus anyone who can speak to deployment options (VPC/private).

Our participants: myself (APAC coordination), Anika (EMEA infra lead), and three architects in NA/West Coast. We tried to find overlap but DST + spread of timezones is making this painful. Can your team do one of these windows (all listed in UTC):
- Option A: 13:00–15:00 UTC (works best for NA morning & EMEA afternoon; awful for APAC)
- Option B: 22:00–00:00 UTC (late EMEA / early APAC — workable for APAC mornings)
- Option C: 01:00–03:00 UTC (straddles APAC morning and NA evening; people in EMEA would be late but might join)

If you can, please propose which option your engineers prefer and who will attend. We can be flexible on the date — target the week of May 31–June 4.

Two asks: 1) confirm slot that gives us a reasonable overlap for our three architect groups; 2) include a short agenda and an ICS invite if we agree.

Thanks,
Oliver
Electrical Engineering Manager
Acme OSS

——

Subject: Re: Engineering workshop — aligning windows across NA/EMEA/APAC

Oliver — thanks for the clear options. Happy to run this workshop.

Quick notes:
- Marissa (SE) and Ben (Solutions) are looped for availability. We commonly anchor larger cross-region sessions to a single UTC block to avoid ambiguous local conversions.
- I put together a 90-minute agenda (attached) and created a short Doodle to capture any firm blackout times: https://doodle.com/poll/tri-region-workshop-abc123

Proposed plan from Redwood:
- Tentatively we prefer Option B (22:00–00:00 UTC). That hits: 15:00 PDT / 18:00 EDT / 00:00 CEST (next day) / 07:00 SGT (next day). It’s late for EMEA but gets APAC into morning and NA during their afternoon/evening.
- If EMEA attendance is mandatory during local business hours, Option A is the fallback and we can rotate a follow-up session targeted at APAC.

I attached a draft agenda (acme-workshop-agenda-v1.pdf) and an .ics I can update once you confirm the final date.

If that works, can you confirm preferred day in the week you mentioned (May 31–June 4)? I’ll lock the calendar and send invites.

—
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Rep, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@acme-oss.com>, Anika Sørensen <anika.sorensen@acme-oss.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Engineering workshop — aligning windows across NA/EMEA/APAC

Looping in a couple constraints from the SE side so we don’t waste calls:
- Our EMEA contacts asked for no meetings that start after 18:30 CEST (they can stay later but prefer not to). That makes Option B (22:00 UTC / 00:00 CEST) awkward for the primary EMEA architect — they would be joining outside their standard hours.
- APAC (SG/HK) folks can do early mornings (06:00–08:00 SGT) but anything before 05:30 is tough.
- DST note: US and EU DST windows line up during May/June (both observing summer time), but when we move dates into Oct/Nov the offsets change and invites that were clear in UTC can produce different local times. Recommend choosing a UTC anchor and clearly showing local times in the calendar invite.

Practical suggestion: pick one 90–120 minute slot anchored to UTC and rotate the follow-up with a second (shorter) session for the region that can’t make the primary time. From experience, the best compromise is a 22:00–00:00 UTC anchor for a single joint session and then a 60-minute APAC-first run one week later for engineers who want a daytime walkthrough.

If we pick 22:00–00:00 UTC, I can cover architecture + deployment options; Ben can run the cost/batching/quantization section. Priyom, I’m available June 2 and June 3 evenings (UTC) from our side.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — 22:00–00:00 UTC sounds acceptable from our side. That gives us the best chance to have all three regional architect groups represented.

We’ll go with Wednesday, June 2 at 22:00–00:00 UTC (please attach as local time so our calendars don’t shift). Also: please include a short pre-read (15 minutes) and call link and indicate whether you’ll share runbooks or a short diagram pack after the session.

I’ll chase internal confirmations if anything changes; go ahead and send the invite.

Best,
Oliver
